title: Each location keeps its own mapping for a category
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Use an organization with two locations, location A and location B, each connected to its own QuickBooks Online company.
  • Have a new No Charge category for this test, category A, with no account at either location.
custom_steps:
1. Work at location A.
  2. Open Integrations > QuickBooks.
  3. Open ShopView Accounts.
  4. Pick an expense account in category A's row.
  5. Click Save.
  6. Switch to location B.
  7. Open Integrations > QuickBooks.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Location A is current.

Step 2:

  • The QuickBooks page opens.

Step 3:

  • Category A's row shows empty.

Step 4:

  • The account shows.

Step 5:

  • The mapping is saved.

Step 6:

  • Location B is current.

Step 7:

  • Category A's row is still empty at location B.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11762 (Story 5, QuickBooks Online account mapping)

  • S5-R6: “The per-category mapping follows the per-row model of part categories, not the fixed ShopView Accounts keys: one row per category per location, keyed by the category's stable key. Archiving a category keeps its mapping; Restore brings it back untouched, nothing is mapped again. The rows exist from the release (S1-R13), so the accountant can map before the setting is on (S5-R5).”
  • S5-R3: “Save stores the mapping for the location. The row and the category dialog (S1-R14) read and write the same mapping, so a change in either place shows in the other. Entries posted to ShopView Review before the row was mapped stay where they are; the accountant reclasses them in QuickBooks.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
